description: Execution evidence that a separate WRITABLE Postgres table (app.case_actions) exists and accepts writes, distinct from the sync-populated read-only mirror tables. Captured live against Lakebase project sentenel-tech-summit-27 on 2026-08-28 via the databricks CLI + psycopg2 (profile fe-sandbox-tech-summit-27-doug, connected as doug.rogers@databricks.com).

write_proof_case_actions.statement: BEGIN; INSERT INTO app.case_actions (payment_id, signal_type, action_type, status, approved_by, audit_trail) VALUES ('PAY-EVIDENCE-CHECK','income_mismatch','hold_for_verification','approved','doug.rogers@databricks.com','[]'::jsonb) RETURNING id, payment_id, action_type, status, approved_by, created_at;
write_proof_case_actions.note: Row was ROLLED BACK so no demo data is polluted — the round-trip proves the table is writable. This is the same write the app's Act layer performs when an examiner approves a disposition.

synced_mirror_contrast.note: The mirror tables (payment_position, open_queue, disposition_recommendations) are populated from Delta by the boot-time sync (app/server/db/sync.ts); the app SELECTs from them and never writes them. case_actions is the sole write-surface.

row_counts_production_branch.note: case_actions is intentionally empty on production/dev between demo runs (wiped by wipeMirroredTables in sync.ts); the mirrors carry 43 flagged payments.
